Theme

Kitchen, meals & drinks

cooking pot noun

also pot, casserole, stockpot, pots and pans

classical

M-O s.v. pan: pot (cacabus)
Varro
Stat. Silv. 4.9.45

1caccabus: short a, double c (Lewis & Short cācabus, taking the heavy first syllable for a long vowel). Greek κάκκαβος. Varro writes caccabum (cited by Lewis & Short); Stat. Silv. 4.9.45, albōrum calicum atque caccabōrum, scans the first syllable heavy, as the double c makes it. Comenius’s cacabīs is marked the same way. Ruling: caccabus: a short a and a double c (provisional).

caccabus1 (cacabus), caccabī m.

noun, second declension

Other words

  • 2ōlla: long o (Lewis & Short leaves it unmarked). The later form of aula: Festus, aulās antīquī dīcēbant, quās nōs dīcimus ōllās. Ruling: ōlla with a long o.

    ōlla2, ōllae f. — pot

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Traupman 124; Traupman 297

    The house spelling.

  • coctōrium, coctōriī n. — casserole

    noun, second declension · also used · modern · Traupman 287

    Not a Lewis & Short headword.

Examples

  • ēlixat ōllīs et cacabīs in focō

    he boils in pots and pans on the hearthComen. OP 54

  • vāsa coquīnāria

    pots and pansTraupman 363

See also saucepan, cook, hearth, kettle, soup, pots and pans.
